adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Betty reports Peter's return to Midtown for the school news and cheers him on, calling him tiger, or rather spider.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A classmate whose return to school Betty reports.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A classmate who cheers his return to school on the school news.
adds.evidence: Theatrical cut: as Peter returns to Midtown, Betty reports it to Midtown News: 'Go get 'em, tiger! Or, should I say, spider.'

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Mr. Dell welcomes Peter back to Midtown as a hero and, with Mr. Harrington, tells him to ignore Coach Wilson calling him a murderer.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A student Dell welcomes back to Midtown as a hero.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Peter's teacher, who welcomes him back to Midtown as a hero.
adds.evidence: Dell and Harrington greet Peter outside their classrooms on his return ('We would love to welcome you back to Midtown High. Where we shape heroes'); when Wilson calls Peter a murderer they tell him not to listen.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Mr. Harrington greets Peter warmly on his return to Midtown, shows him a display case made in his honor and tells him to ignore Coach Wilson.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Peter's teacher, who shows him a display case in his honor.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A student Harrington welcomes back with a display case in his honor.
adds.evidence: Harrington builds a display case with their Venice photo, shows it to Peter on his return, and calls Wilson a conspiracy theorist to ignore.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Mr. Dell and Mr. Harrington greet Peter together on his return to Midtown and tell him to ignore Coach Wilson.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A fellow teacher who welcomes Peter back with Dell.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: A fellow teacher who welcomes Peter back with Harrington.
adds.evidence: Dell and Harrington greet Peter together outside their classrooms and both tell him not to listen to Wilson.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Flash cuts Ned off in front of the crowd outside Midtown to call himself Spider-Man's best friend and plug his book, and Ned walks off annoyed.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: A classmate who claims to be Peter's best friend over Ned.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Peter's best friend, whom Flash talks over to plug his book.
adds.evidence: When a protester asks Ned who he is, Flash interrupts to say he is Spider-Man's best friend and advertises Flashpoint, causing Ned to walk off in annoyance.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Jameson blames Spider-Man for the destruction at Happy's building and May's death. Peter calls in to his broadcast to admit he brought the villains and say where he will be.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: The hero Jameson blames for May's death, who calls in to his broadcast.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: The broadcaster who blames Peter for May's death and airs his call.
adds.evidence: Jameson reports from the destroyed condo that Spider-Man is responsible for the destruction and May's death; Peter later calls in via video broadcast admitting he brought the perpetrators and revealing the Statue of Liberty.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Happy barges into Peter's bedroom at the Parkers' apartment and finds MJ there with Peter, just as the news of Peter's identity surrounds the building.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Peter's girlfriend, whom Happy finds in Peter's room.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: The man who barges into Peter's room and finds MJ there.
adds.evidence: Opening scene: Hogan insists on checking a noise and opens Peter's bedroom door to find Peter and MJ, who came in through the window; they then watch the NY1 report together.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: May and Ned are brought in together to the police precinct for Damage Control's questioning, walking past Peter's room on the way.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Peter's best friend, brought in for questioning with May.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Peter's aunt, brought in for questioning with Ned.
adds.evidence: May is asked to come to the precinct and meets Ned and MJ, who were called in too; they pass Peter's room together and she tells him not to talk without a lawyer.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Sadie Deever is among the Damage Control agents watching as Cleary interrogates Ned and MJ.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: An agent who watches his interrogation of Ned and MJ.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: The agent leading the interrogation she watches.
adds.evidence: Uncredited: Deever oversees Cleary's interrogations of MJ and Ned (confirmed by the actress); no lines between them.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Stranded in a strange world, Eddie decides to go meet Spider-Man while Venom would rather go skinny dipping. They are pulled back home, leaving a piece of Venom behind.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: The symbiote stranded with Eddie, who wants a swim instead.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Venom's host, stranded with him in a strange world.
adds.evidence: Mid-credits scene: at a bar, Eddie wants to go to New York to meet Spider-Man, Venom suggests skinny dipping, then they are transported back, leaving a symbiote fragment.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Betty interviews Mr. Harrington about Peter for the school news, and he admits his ex-wife now believes the Mysterio theories.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Betty's teacher, whom she interviews about Peter.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Harrington's student, who interviews him about Peter.
adds.evidence: Extended cut only ('The More Fun Stuff Version'): Betty interviews Harrington about being Peter's teacher and the Mysterio theories; not in the theatrical cut.

adds.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
adds.text: Betty interviews Mr. Dell about Peter for the school news, and he tells her what he would be if he were Spider-Man.
adds.on_a_card_about_b: Betty's history teacher, whom she interviews about Peter.
adds.on_b_card_about_a: Dell's student, who interviews him about Peter.
adds.evidence: Extended cut only ('The More Fun Stuff Version'): Betty interviews her history teacher Dell, who tells her what he would be if he was Spider-Man; not in the theatrical cut.

owner_calls.question: Two stages rest only on the extended cut (Spider-Man: No Way Home, The More Fun Stuff Version): Betty interviewing Harrington and Dell for the school news. Count extended-cut scenes as part of the film?
owner_calls.evidence: Betty's interviews of Harrington and Dell are cited to SMNWHTMFSV only.

owner_calls.question: Sadie Deever's appearance is an uncredited background role at Cleary's interrogations, confirmed by the actress. Keep the stage?
owner_calls.evidence: Fandom lists her as uncredited, citing the actress's post; no lines with Cleary.
